$comment: Each lane's Postgres connection limit, with its source, plus the connection sources the hub opens. Read by tests/test_database_connection_ceiling.py, which computes every deploy path's worst case from the real deploy config and fails above ceiling_fraction of the limit. Raising max_connections or the tier restarts the instance: that is the owner's decision, never a side effect of editing this file.

rollout_overlap.source: Cloud Run: 'Because the maximum instances limit is a limit for each revision, during a deployment, the total number of instances for the service can exceed the maximum instances per revision' (https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/about-instance-autoscaling). Measured: 10 active consent-protocol instances summed across revisions with max 5, dev on 2026-10-05 and UAT on 2026-10-01 (run.googleapis.com/container/instance_count).

superuser_reserved_connections.source: PostgreSQL 15 default superuser_reserved_connections = 3 (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/15/runtime-config-connection.html). No instance overrides it (gcloud sql instances describe, 2026-10-06).

hushh_mcp/services/market_cache_store.py.why: Market refresh advisory lock. The startup warm and the refresh loop run one after the other, so one connection per worker at a time.

hushh_mcp/services/fleet_sweep_lock.py.why: Pod liveness and personal-agent reconcile sweeps. Every hub worker tries both locks, and each try opens a connection, even though only the holder keeps it.

listener_modules.$comment: Each module holds one connection per worker for the process lifetime, drawn from that worker's asyncpg pool (pool.acquire then LISTEN). The request floor is pool size minus these.

dev.max_connections_source: Tier default: 3.75 GB to under 6 GB gives 100 (https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/flags, max_connections). No max_connections flag is set (gcloud sql instances describe hushh-dev-pg, 2026-10-06).

external_reserve.source: About 20 of dev's 99 backends at the 2026-10-01/02 peak came from outside the deployed config: local backends run at code defaults, 35 connections per process (asyncpg DB_POOL_MAX_SIZE 20 in db/connection.py, SQLAlchemy pool 5 plus overflow 10 in db/db_client.py).
